name: IEC magnitude comparator (COMP)
summary: IEC COMP element comparing two binary words P and Q, with outputs for P>Q, P=Q and P<Q.
description: The IEC magnitude comparator is marked COMP. Its inputs are grouped as word P and word Q with binary weights, and its outputs are labelled P>Q, P=Q and P<Q. Cascading inputs carry the same labels in a separate group so that comparators can be chained for longer words.

Digital comparators appear in set-point logic, address matching and limit checking. A reviewer should confirm the bit order of P and Q, because a swapped weight produces a comparison that is correct only for some values.
The symbol does not indicate whether the comparison is for signed or unsigned numbers. Standard devices compare unsigned binary.
readingNotes: Check bit weights on both words.
Cascade inputs are needed for words longer than one device.
drawingChecklist: Group and weight the P and Q inputs.
distinction: An analogue voltage comparator compares two voltages, not binary words.
